description: Fix github issue #91: `opentabs tool call` cannot accept JSON payloads larger than the OS argv limit (~1 MB on macOS), so tools that accept inline binary/text content (base64 images, large pasted text, document bodies) cannot be invoked from the CLI. The server-side /tools/:name/call HTTP endpoint already accepts arbitrary-size bodies — this is purely a CLI UX bug in platform/cli/src/commands/tool.ts where the only inputs to handleToolCall are (a) the positional [json] argument and (b) the --params <json> flag, both of which go through argv. Resolve it at the platform level by adding a --params-file <path> flag that reads JSON from a file path, with `-` meaning stdin. This matches standard Unix idioms (kubectl apply -f, gh api --input, jq -f) and is unambiguous — no magic `@` prefix that would collide with valid JSON strings beginning with `@` (e.g. `'@mention'`). After this PRD lands: users can pass multi-MB payloads via `opentabs tool call TOOL --params-file payload.json`, pipe JSON over stdin via `cat payload.json | opentabs tool call TOOL --params-file -`, get clear conflict errors if they combine --params-file with --params or the positional argument, and receive path-qualified error messages when the file is missing or contains invalid JSON. A unit test covers argument parsing and file reading; an E2E test invokes a real plugin tool with a >1 MB payload through the CLI subprocess to prove the argv limit is actually bypassed end-to-end.

userStories.title: Add --params-file flag to `opentabs tool call` with file and stdin support
userStories.description: Extend handleToolCall in platform/cli/src/commands/tool.ts to accept a new --params-file <path> option. When <path> is `-`, read JSON from process.stdin (bypassing argv entirely). When <path> is any other string, read the file from disk via node:fs/promises readFile. Validate that the user supplied at most one input source across positional jsonArg, --params, and --params-file; exit with a clear error if multiple are given. Path-qualify JSON parse errors so 'Invalid JSON in /path/to/payload.json' is easier to debug than the current 'Invalid JSON: <500KB of blob>'. Register the new option on the commander subcommand with an example in the addHelpText block.
acceptanceCriteria: `opentabs tool call TOOL --params-file payload.json` reads and parses JSON from payload.json and sends it to POST /tools/TOOL/call
`opentabs tool call TOOL --params-file -` reads JSON from process.stdin until EOF and sends it
Supplying more than one of {positional jsonArg, --params, --params-file} exits code 2 with stderr message 'Specify only one of: [json], --params, --params-file'
A missing --params-file path exits code 2 with stderr starting 'Failed to read params file <path>:' and the underlying node fs error message

Invalid JSON from --params-file exits code 2 with stderr 'Invalid JSON in <path>:' (or 'Invalid JSON on stdin:' for --params-file -) followed by the JSON.parse error message; the raw blob is NOT echoed
handleToolCall signature adds `paramsFile?: string` to its options parameter
The commander .option() call reads '--params-file <path>' with description 'Read tool arguments as JSON from a file path (use - for stdin). Bypasses the argv size limit.'
addHelpText for `tool call` includes a new example line: `$ opentabs tool call <tool> --params-file payload.json` and `$ cat payload.json | opentabs tool call <tool> --params-file -`
Existing callers of handleToolCall that pass only positional jsonArg or --params continue to behave identically (no regression)
--instance and --tab-id options continue to merge into args after the JSON source is parsed, regardless of which source was used

userStories.title: Add unit tests for --params-file argument handling in tool.ts
userStories.description: Add a new platform/cli/src/commands/tool.test.ts file with Vitest unit tests that exercise the argument-parsing and file-reading logic added in US-001. The tests must cover: reading JSON from a file path, reading JSON from stdin (simulated with a Readable stream), mutual exclusion between positional/--params/--params-file, missing file errors, invalid JSON errors with path-qualified messages, and the large-payload happy path (>2 MB). Export the readParamsSource helper from tool.ts so it can be imported by the test. Do NOT spawn the real CLI subprocess — that is covered by the existing cli-smoke.test.ts and the E2E test in US-003. This story is pure unit-level logic validation.
acceptanceCriteria: File platform/cli/src/commands/tool.test.ts exists with a `describe('readParamsSource', ...)` block
Test: reading a JSON file returns { json: <contents>, origin: <path> }
Test: reading with paramsFile='-' reads from a provided Readable and returns { json, origin: 'stdin' } (use a mock / stubbed process.stdin)
Test: supplying two of {jsonArg, params, paramsFile} causes process.exit(2) and writes 'Specify only one of:' to stderr
Test: missing file path causes process.exit(2) with stderr containing 'Failed to read params file' and the path
Test: reading a 2 MB JSON file round-trips without truncation (verify length and SHA-256 of the parsed payload's base64 field matches the input)
readParamsSource is exported from platform/cli/src/commands/tool.ts so the test can import it
The test file does not spawn a subprocess or start a real server
Tests run under Vitest and pass on node 22+

userStories.title: Add E2E test invoking a plugin tool with a >1 MB payload via CLI subprocess
userStories.description: Add platform/cli/src/tool-call-large-payload.e2e.ts that spawns the real `opentabs` CLI as a subprocess with a payload larger than the macOS ARG_MAX limit (~1 MB). The test asserts: (a) passing the payload via --params-file succeeds, (b) passing the same payload via --params fails with E2BIG / argv limit errors on macOS and Linux, proving the regression is gone. The test uses the existing E2E fixture infrastructure — spawn MCP server, load the e2e-test plugin which has the `echo` tool, send a payload where message is a 1.5 MB base64 string. Verify the echoed response round-trips the full string intact.
acceptanceCriteria: File e2e/tool-call-large-payload.e2e.ts exists and is reachable by npx playwright test
Test: piping a 1.5 MB JSON payload through --params-file succeeds, the CLI exits code 0, and stdout contains the echoed message of exact length 1.5*1024*1024
Test: reading a 1.5 MB JSON file via --params-file <path> succeeds with the same round-trip assertion
Test: attempting to pass the same 1.5 MB JSON inline via --params fails at process spawn (or at commander's argv read) — the test explicitly documents and asserts this to prevent regression
The test uses setupToolTest from e2e/helpers.ts to stand up the MCP server with the e2e-test plugin (which exposes e2e-test_echo)
The test spawns the CLI via the platform/cli/dist/cli.js binary with OPENTABS_CONFIG_DIR pointing to the fixture's ephemeral config so the test is isolated
The test reads the auth secret from the fixture's temp dir and passes it through env so the CLI authenticates against the fixture server
The test cleans up the tmp file and CLI subprocess in afterAll / afterEach
The test does not call pkill/killall — it kills only its own spawned child processes
